rationale: This targets the largest remaining error in the B3a report (§5.4, §7, largest_remaining_error): confident noisy bona false alarms, half of them English. On the half_B merge, English is 258 of 782 noisy bona but carries 91 of 180 false alarms. English R_bona is 67.4 matched / 62.0 heldout, against zh 84.7 / 81.3. Full-set English EER did not improve at the merge (matched 12.76 -> 13.66) and rose at ep8 on all three sets. The gap is not new. The B2 wave summary says English bona recall never moved in that wave, and B3a's consistency removed only 4 English false alarms (95 -> 91) against 29 Chinese ones (118 -> 89). The skill says that when a lever's target did not move, the next step should be a different mechanism, not a higher dose. Consistency already hit heldout, matched and noisy EER; it missed English and the saturated core. So I am trying the untested exposure mechanism rather than --consistency_lambda 1.0 (analyst rank 2). The analyst ranked this lever first, and it is in the wave.json lever_queue (sampler_balanced) and in the approved plan. Only the English bona exposure should change, not the operating point. The B3a merge is already optimal at 0.5 (best global logit -0.15, recoverable 0.02, report §5.2), so the CE weights are re-derived from train_label.txt to keep the effective bona:spoof weight at 2.1028:1, as lever_notes require. The four flags are one coupled group in wave.json, and every other B3a flag is kept, including consistency js 0.3 at --batch_size 8. Run length is unchanged: 8 epochs, within max_epochs 10, and the same 75792 steps. A seed repeat is not warranted while untested configuration levers that the evidence supports remain.
hypothesis: The en-zh bona gap is an exposure problem. English bona are only 2,922 of 75,785 training clips (3.9 %), English is 23.2 % of training data, and P(bona|en)=0.1665 against 0.1965 for zh. Consistency cannot fix this, because the two views of an English bona clip agree with each other while being wrong together. A class- and language-balanced draw (each class half en / half zh, bona_frac 0.5) shows each English bona clip about 6.5x per epoch at an unchanged effective class prior (CE 0.3223/0.6777). That should move English bona out of the saturated spoof region and improve the ranking of English bona against spoof. Neither the global operating point nor Chinese / clean behaviour should move.

header_text:
B3b = B3a + class- and language-balanced sampling: --sampler balanced --sampler_lang_balance --sampler_bona_frac 0.5 --ce_weights 0.3223 0.6777. The four flags are one coupled group, and the CE weights are re-derived from train_label.txt so the effective bona:spoof weight of 0.1/0.9 at 18.94 % bona (2.1028:1) is unchanged. Everything else is identical to B3a: consistency js 0.3 with pairs=both, --batch_size 8 = 16 clips/step, 8 epochs, LR 2.5e-6 cosine to 5e-7, loudness norm -23. The sampler draws len(dataset) items per epoch, so steps and the schedule are unchanged (~8 h).

Evidence (B3a report, docs/experiments-exploration/b3-experiments/20261010_143058_B3a_*.md): English is 258 of 782 half_B noisy bona but 91 of 180 merge false alarms. English R_bona is 67.4 / 62.0 (matched / heldout), against zh 84.7 / 81.3. English EER did not improve under consistency. The merge operating point is already optimal (one global shift recovers 0.02), so the remaining error is ranking, not calibration.

Target: English bona exposure. Each English bona clip is drawn ~6.5x per epoch; zh spoof drops to 0.40x.

Rule against B3a-top5 = 93.06 on half_B: promote if the delta is > +0.5, the CI excludes 0 and the clean drop is <= 0.5; null within +-0.5; negative below -0.5.
